correctness.rationale: Conditioning on one persistent uniform phase yields Q_m=(1/P)∫(1-h(theta)/W)^m dtheta. Translated circular interval overlap h has exact plateau heights a=max(0,W+ell-P), b=min(W,ell), plateau phase-lengths |P-W-ell|, |W-ell| and two linear ramps; direct integration proves the full formula with all boundary cases. Endpoint dominance yields positive missed-phase floor, order 1/m critical law and geometric law; a=c_+/m near critical yields the stated crossover. Jensen strict convexity for m>=2 proves uniquely optimal full-phase randomization. The model is exact with no unproved infinite inference; 668 supplementary computational assertions checked from packaged checker.

originality.rationale: Search and inspected-literature comparison did not reveal the exact restricted-start uniform-jitter shared-phase non-detection law or its positive-floor/inverse-effort/geometric trichotomy. Michel et al. evaluate fixed recurrent sampling phases, Balantic–Donovan optimize adaptive schedules with hourly vocal availability, and classical full-circle random-arc coverage asks different questions. The independence-conditioning identity and Jensen inequality are routine and are not claimed novel; the evaluated formula, boundary and crossover are the claim. Best-knowledge, not certified historical priority.
residual_risks: Older random-circle coverage may contain an unstated broader result reducing to the restricted-arc finite formula; full text of Siegel and Holst (1982) not inspected.

The model omits drift, dropped calls, false-positive identification, energy costs and physical overlap budgets.

value.rationale: A quantitative duty-cycle aliasing blind spot motivates the restricted phase window: identical listening lengths and re-randomization over cycles can either permanently fail for a positive fraction of persistent call phases, attain only 1/m improvement at exact coverage, or attain exponential reliability. Exact finite probabilities, a sharp worst-case distinction and near-critical scaling supply actionable benchmark insights for choosing whether a recorder needs full-period timing variation. Such qualitative risk-regime distinction is not a mere normalization/type check; no field calibration is asserted.
